Behind him a huge translucent bubble (about human height) wears a discarded suit jacket draped over its curve and uses a glove-like protrusion to pull cash out of an open wallet on a nearby table. The bubble holds a small stack of bills and a clipboard made of bubble-sheen, counting them with a brass coin counter. Only two main figures: Griffin at the podium and the anthropomorphic bubble taking money and tallying it.
Visual turn to show in the drawing: The expected roles are reversed: instead of the investor controlling investments, the bubble is actively extracting and counting Griffin's money — the investment has become the investor.
Depict this visible ironic reversal, not a literal reenactment of the reported event or a generic portrait. The turn must read without the title. A metaphor must not assert an unreported action or guilt.

Strongly reference the pen-and-ink editorial cartoon work of Georges Bigot, Charles Wirgman and Charles Keene: observant human caricature, expressive faces and gestures, lively economical contours with deliberate changes in line weight, convincing clothing folds, and sparse hand-drawn hatching. Make these nineteenth-century draughtsmen the primary visual references throughout the drawing.
